items.title: Mac McClung begins international career after winning pair of G League MVP awards, 3 NBA Slam Dunk Contests
items.content:
Mac McClung has appeared in 17 total NBA games since going undrafted out of Texas Tech in 2021. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images)Scott Taetsch via Getty ImagesMac McClung is the all-time leading scorer in the G League, where he became the first player to win multiple MVP awards. The 6-foot-2 guard's viral hops carried over to the pros, so much so that he found himself a regular contributor in the NBA's All-Star Weekend, during which he was crowned as a three-time Slam Dunk Contest champion. His acrobatics vaulted him to a three-peat in the event.

Unfortunately for McClung, despite his accolades and unquestioned drive, he hasn't been able to carve out a long-term role in the NBA.

Now 27, McClung is headed overseas to begin an international career. He has signed with Spain's Bàsquet Girona in the Liga ACB, the club announced on Thursday.

✅💣 En @McclungMac és gironí. Benvingut a Fontajau! ❤️🤍 pic.twitter.com/3PNEoOLNgR

— FIATC Girona (@BasquetGirona) August 6, 2026Bàsquet Girona was founded in 2014 by three-time NBA All-Star and one-time NBA champion Marc Gasol, who serves as the club's president.

McClung burst onto the scene as a popular prospect from Gate City, Virginia, the origin of his eye-catching highlight mixtapes. He went on to play at Georgetown and Texas Tech. He was part of a Red Raiders team that earned a No. 6 seed in the 2021 NCAA tournament before bowing out in the Round of 32.

Then he went undrafted. Since, he's been grinding in the G League, earning a handful of fleeting NBA opportunities along the way.

McClung has appeared in a total of 17 NBA games, suiting up for five franchises: The Chicago Bulls, Los Angeles Lakers, Philadelphia 76ers, Orlando Magic and Indiana Pacers. 

Of those 17 games he's logged minutes in, 11 came this past season. Early in the 2025-26 campaign, the guard-needy Pacers signed McClung to a multi-year deal — his first standard NBA contract — except they waived him less than two weeks later. McClung played in three games for the Pacers, all losses. He averaged 6.3 points, 1.3 rebounds and 1.7 steals off the bench.

He returned to Chicago, where he put on a show for the G League's Windy City Bulls and got eight games worth of run with the NBA's Bulls. He notably surpassed Renaldo Major for the most career G League points amid a 59-point outburst in March en route to earning MVP honors. He first won MVP with the Osceola Magic during the 2023-24 campaign. The season before that, he claimed a G League title with the Delaware Blue Coats.

Just as he did with the G League's Magic two seasons ago, McClung took home the scoring title this time around with the G League's Bulls. He led the league with 31.8 points per game, plus he averaged 7.9 assists while making 3.5 triples per contest.

items.title: Naz Reid Focuses On Role As Leader After Being Traded To Hornets
items.content:
Naz Reid was one of the Timberwolves‘ most popular players during his time with the franchise, so it’s been hard for Minnesota fans to get used to the idea that he’s now wearing a Hornets uniform. Reid, who was sent to Charlotte as part of the return in the LaMelo Ball trade, talks about the loyalty he generated and several other topics in an interview with Roderick Boone of The Charlotte Observer (subscription required).

“It’s kind of dedication and testament to my work. They’ve seen it since Day 1,” Reid said. “I mentioned it all the time. They’ve seen me go undrafted, they’ve seen me work my way to some playing time minutes — whether it’s 15 minutes a game, 10 minutes a game — and they’ve seen me working my way to it going to 20 minutes and so forth and so on. So, Sixth Man of the Year, I couldn’t have that without those fans and the situation I was in. I’m definitely excited to share that moment with them. 

“And then obviously having the moment of me being traded and then them expressing their feelings about how much they wish I was able to stay and so forth and so on. So, it’s just kudos to that fan base. And like I said, the way they appreciated me, the way that they’ve embraced me since Day 1. I worked with them for eight years, and each year wasn’t easy. Each year was tough. It got better, obviously. They’ve been in situations where stands weren’t filled to where they are now. And I’ve been in that same element with them. Being the longest-tenured player there, they’ve seen the work that I put in for eight years. And they kind of, I guess, appreciated that.”

Reid began his career on a two-way deal with the Wolves after going undrafted out of LSU in 2019. He appeared in just 30 games as a rookie, but from there he was able to work his way into a steady spot in the team’s rotation. He won Sixth Man of the Year honors in 2024 and finished fifth and fourth in the balloting the past two seasons.

Reid provided a steady inside presence off the bench as the primary backup to Rudy Gobert, Karl-Anthony Towns and more recently Julius Randle. He’s expected to move into a starting spot with the Hornets, replacing Miles Bridges, who was traded to Phoenix last month.

Reid was part of numerous high-level playoff games in Minnesota, including two trips to the Western Conference finals, and he plans to share the lessons from that experience with his new Charlotte teammates, many of whom got their first taste of NBA success last season.

“As me being the leader or one of the oldest guys, kind of knowing what playoff experience feels like and knowing what that environment is like and knowing what it is like, or knowing how it feels for a state to embrace you, let alone at the highest level,” Reid said. “So, I think just being able to put my head down, going to work, and obviously leading by example, not just by words.
